$comment: Names that scripts/audit-blocklist.mjs would otherwise report as suspected
false positives, because they still resolve on the npm registry with a real
release history, but which are deliberately blocked anyway.
Every entry needs a written reason of at least 10 characters; the script
refuses to run otherwise. A reason must say WHAT justifies blocking every
version, not merely that someone decided to.
The bar: an upstream malware advisory (GHSA + OSV MAL-) that classifies the
WHOLE package as malicious is sufficient. A vendor blog post naming specific
poisoned releases is NOT - that is a hijack, and hijacks get version pins.
Entries here should be revisited when an advisory is withdrawn. Reviewed

names.ecinc-cloud-moaxmpp: GHSA-65hf-ffjr-7wpg / MAL-2025-6214 classifies the entire package as malware. 65 versions over 731 days, so the audit flags it, but the advisory covers all versions rather than a release range. Most uncomfortable entry in this file: worth re-checking if the advisory is ever withdrawn.
names.uol-simple-api-futebol: GHSA-cmw3-w7ff-wvjv / MAL-2026-6087 classifies the entire package as malware, with no version range narrowing it.
names.custom-save-area-block: GHSA-qjmg-vm87-pgxf / MAL-2026-6152 classifies the entire package as malware. Dormant since 2024-05-20, so a name block cannot collide with new legitimate releases.
names.personal-custom-button: GHSA-rc5f-67q5-hfv2 / MAL-2026-6171 classifies the entire package as malware. Same maintainer and same dormancy as custom-save-area-block.
names.0e: GHSA-ch8j-x95h-wqcv / MAL-2025-49456 classifies the entire package as malware. Dormant since 2021-11-12.
names.claude-cup: GHSA-r663-w5qf-3552 / MAL-2026-5789 classifies the entire package as malware. The 42 releases inside 36 days are the campaign itself, not a legitimate history.
